title: Structure and Organization of Full-Length Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor in Extracellular Vesicles by Cryo-Electron Tomography
content: Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) is essential for normal development, but abnormal EGFR activity is associated with several human cancers and is the target of many anticancer therapies. Previous structural studies of EGFR and related receptors have led to many valuable insights into EGFR function, but key questions remain: Whether and how structural information beyond dimerization is communicated from the extracellular to intracellular regions of the receptor; what roles EGFR multimers other than the active-state dimer might play in signaling continue to attract interest.
